The repo contains a bunch of pre-built binaries, which seems concerning. Are they freely distributed?
Yes, the pre-built binaries in the repo are covered under the MIT License, as noted in the LICENSE file. They are freely distributable.

Can you please rather package it as a proper python application:

https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/tutorials/packaging-projects/
I'll look into it.

@andrew@codeconstruct.com.au, Can we install only the "*.py" files and keep "keys/" and "prebuilt/" outside the package? These contain board-specific binaries and keys that are meant to be customizable or replaceable externally.
Sounds good to me, but so long as it's done using the usual python packaging methods.
Please review V4 again when you have a chance. Thanks.
Done
Why are we installing pre-built binaries? I'm not in favour.

Currently, these pre-built binaries are using for bootmcu-spl to bootup AST2700. We use fmc-imgtool to generate BOOTMCU_FW_BINARY = "ast2700-ibex-spl.bin". So, we put the pre-built binaries at fmc-imgtool.
```
ast2700-caliptra-fw.bin  ddr4_2d_pmu_train_dmem.bin  ddr4_2d_pmu_train_imem.bin  ddr4_pmu_train_dmem.bin  ddr4_pmu_train_imem.bin  ddr5_pmu_train_dmem.bin  ddr5_pmu_train_imem.bin  dp_fw.bin  uefi_ast2700.bin
```

I moved prebuilt binaries to fmc-images.bb. Refer to 
https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/openbmc/+/82105
Please review again when you have a chance. Thanks.
